data.exact_reserve_text: During 2015, net ultimate claims in respect of prior underwriting years (2014 & prior) increased by GBP 0.8m. This was mainly due to the Accident & Health class which saw an increase in exposure/written premium in the 2014 underwriting year. The General Liability and Offshore Energy classes also contributed to an increase in prior underwriting year net ultimate claims during 2015, as a result of large losses in these classes. These increases were more than offset by reductions due to favourable claims experience, most notably in Onshore Energy, but also Energy Casualty and Aerospace.

data.standardized_narrative: Using the gross claims development triangle, cumulative estimates for underwriting years prior to 2014 produced a net favourable movement (release) of approximately GBP 10.3m in 2015 (c. -2.18% of opening gross claims outstanding). However the report's narrative states that net ultimate claims for prior years (2014 & prior) increased by GBP 0.8m (net of reinsurance), driven by Accident & Health exposure increases and large losses in General Liability and Offshore Energy, partly offset by favourable experience in Onshore Energy, Energy Casualty and Aerospace. In summary, there were both adverse and favourable developments across classes (mixed direction); gross-triangle analysis indicates an overall release while the narrative reports a small net adverse movement on a net (post-reinsurance) basis.

data.data_quality_notes: Gross prior-year movement was calculated from the printed GROSS claims development triangle (pages 37-38). The narrative on page 38 reports a NET adverse movement of GBP 0.8m (net of reinsurance). No explicit gross 'movement in prior year provision' GROSS figure was printed in a single movement note; therefore gross PYD was derived from the triangle (confidence 0.8). This produces a different sign/amount to the report's net figure (NET = +0.8m). Amounts presented are in the report's native units (GBP 000 converted to millions).
